# AD compromise is an edge path, not a single bug

## Claim

A user has a right over an object that leads to another right, then to a session on a high-value host.

## Test

Collect with BloodHound. Read the ACL edges. Pick the shortest path to the objective and prove one edge.

## Proof

A password reset, ticket or session that grants the next node, with the path in BloodHound.

## Failure modes

A roastable account with a strong password is not a finding until cracked. A path that needs DA to start is circular.

failure: A roastable account with a strong password is not a finding until cracked. A path that needs DA to start is circular.

# Desync needs two HTTP parsers and an ambiguous length

## Claim

A front end and back end disagree about where a request ends, usually through Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding or HTTP/2 downgrade.

## Test

Send ambiguous requests. Try CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE, CRLF header injection and HTTP/2 pseudo-header tricks. Confirm with timing and a second client.

## Proof

A second clean client receives the wrong response, or a repeatable timing signal.

## Failure modes

One 400 does not prove desync. Shared proxies make results non-deterministic.

# GraphQL authorization is per field, not per endpoint

## Claim

The gateway checks the query but resolvers do not check the object, field or mutation. Introspection is a map, not a finding.

## Test

Test each field and mutation with two roles. Test node lookups, nested fields, aliases, batching and cost limits.

## Proof

A restricted field or mutation returns data for a lower-privilege account.

## Failure modes

Introspection enabled is not a bug. HTTP 200 with GraphQL errors is not success.

# Password reset trusts the request host

## Claim

The reset link is built from Host, X-Forwarded-Host or Forwarded without an allowlist.

## Test

Request a reset with each header set to a controlled domain. Check the email and exchange the token.

A reflected host in the page is not the same as a host used in email. Proxies normalize.

# IDOR is a missing owner check, not a hidden id

## Claim

An object id from the request is used without comparing the object owner to the session user. Hiding the id in a UUID does not add a check.

## Test

Create two accounts at the same role. Capture an object id from A. Request it with B. Repeat for read, update, delete and export.

## Proof

B receives or changes A's object, with both sessions and the ids in the log.

## Failure modes

A public object, a 200 with an empty body, or an admin bypass is not the same bug. Check the data, not the status.

# JWT bugs are claim trust, not base64

## Claim

The verifier trusts an algorithm, key or claim it should not. Decoding is not verification.

## Test

Test alg none, algorithm confusion, weak HMAC keys, kid injection, jku/x5u, claim type confusion and expiry handling.

## Proof

A forged token accepted by a protected endpoint.

## Failure modes

A decoded payload is not a finding. A 401 with a different body can still be a bypass on a sibling route.

# OAuth redirect matching is prefix logic under pressure

## Claim

The authorization server compares redirect URIs with loose rules. Path traversal, a subdomain, an open redirect or a fragment can move the code.

## Test

Map every redirect URI and the matching rule. Test path, query, fragment, subdomain, case and open redirect on an allowed host. Reuse state and nonce.

## Proof

A code or token delivered to an attacker-controlled origin, then exchanged for a session.

## Failure modes

A login CSRF needs a victim action. A code for your own account is not account takeover.

# Prototype pollution needs a merge sink and a gadget

## Claim

A recursive merge writes __proto__ or constructor.prototype, and a later lookup reads an inherited property.

## Test

Send __proto__ and constructor.prototype objects to JSON merge endpoints. Look for a gadget in config or auth.

## Proof

An inherited property changes behavior, such as a role or a header.

## Failure modes

A polluted Object.prototype without a gadget has no impact. JSON.parse alone does not pollute.

# A race is a check and a write without one lock

## Claim

The invariant is checked before a write, with no transaction or unique constraint. Parallel requests pass the same check.

## Test

Identify the invariant. Send parallel requests, ideally in one packet on HTTP/2. Compare successes with the intended limit.

## Proof

Two successes where one was allowed, with timestamps and request ids.

## Failure modes

A retry looks like a race. Server deduplication may hide it on a later request.

# SQL injection is a string-built query at a boundary

## Claim

User input reaches a query without a parameter binding. Escaping can fail when the charset, collation or parser changes.

## Test

Establish true and false baselines. Test quote, comment and parenthesis behavior. Move to time or OOB only when union and error are blocked.

## Proof

A bounded extraction of a value the tester should not see, with request and response.

## Failure modes

A WAF block looks like a false condition. Network jitter looks like a time delay. Do not dump the database.

# SSRF hides in URL parser disagreement

## Claim

One component validates a URL and another fetches it. Different parsers disagree about host, scheme, userinfo or path.

## Test

Use a listener to confirm the fetch. Test http:///host, backslashes, userinfo, encoded delimiters, IPv4-mapped IPv6, decimal IPs, redirects and DNS rebinding.

## Proof

A callback from the target, or a response body from an internal service.

## Failure modes

DNS-only SSRF is weak without exfiltration. A hit on your listener does not prove the response reaches the attacker.

failure: DNS-only SSRF is weak without exfiltration. A hit on your listener does not prove the response reaches the attacker.

# Traversal is a join before canonicalization

## Claim

The app joins a user path to a root without resolving and checking the result. Encoded separators and absolute second arguments bypass naive filters.

## Test

Try ../, ..%2f, double encoding, absolute paths, null bytes and Windows separators. Compare the served file with the intended root.

## Proof

A file outside the intended directory is returned or written.

## Failure modes

Reflected filenames are not traversal. A 404 with the path in the body proves nothing.

Extension, MIME, magic bytes and the serving path are checked inconsistently, or the stored file is executable.

## Claim

A sanitizer, template engine or WAF reads the input with a different parser than the browser. The gap is the payload space.

Map the sanitizer and the sink. Try mXSS, namespace changes, comment tricks, attribute boundaries and encoding that normalizes late.

A payload that fires in an innerHTML test may not fire in the page. A CSP report without execution is not a finding.

# A weak service ACL is local privilege escalation

## Claim

A service binary or its directory is writable by a low-privilege user, or the service path is unquoted.

## Test

Check service ACLs and binary paths. Look for unquoted paths with spaces. Replace the binary and restart if allowed.

## Proof

A shell as the service account, usually SYSTEM.

## Failure modes

A writable directory is not enough if the binary is signed and locked. Restart rights matter.
